Wizzynow
Gothic Quarter

Narrow stone lanes around the cathedral, on the site of the Roman town.

The must-sees

11 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Church

    Barcelona Cathedral

    It is dedicated to the Holy Cross and to Saint Eulàlia, a young martyr of the city. The ornate main facade was only added in the late 19th century, centuries after the interior.

    Look for

    Down the steps in the crypt under the high altar lies Saint Eulàlia’s alabaster sarcophagus.

  2. 02
    Building · 1906

    Casa Batlló

    Gaudí remodelled an existing apartment block for the Batlló family between 1904 and 1906. Many read the roof and the tower with its cross as Saint George slaying the dragon.

    Look for

    Next door stands Puig i Cadafalch’s Casa Amatller with its stepped gable: rival architects side by side on what was nicknamed the Block of Discord.

  3. 03
    Building · 1912

    Casa Milà (La Pedrera)

    Gaudí built it for Pere Milà and Roser Segimon between 1906 and 1912. Locals mocked its rough stone face as “the quarry”, and the nickname stuck.

    Look for

    The balcony railings, twisted like seaweed, were worked in wrought iron by Gaudí’s collaborator Josep Maria Jujol.

  4. 04
    Neighbourhood

    Gothic Quarter

    Roman Barcino stood here, and pieces of its walls still show between later buildings. Some of the neo-Gothic touches were added in the early 20th century to make the quarter look more medieval.

    Look for

    In Carrer del Paradís, step into a courtyard to find four Roman columns of the Temple of Augustus.

  5. 05
    Market

    La Boqueria Market

    The covered market was built in the 19th century on the site of the convent of Sant Josep, which gives it its official name. Market stalls had gathered at this spot long before.

    Look for

    Look up at the iron entrance arch on La Rambla, with coloured glass and the name Mercat de Sant Josep.

  6. 06
    Neighbourhood

    La Rambla

    It follows the line of a seasonal stream that once ran outside the medieval walls. Today it is a chain of stretches, each with its own name, together called Les Rambles.

    Look for

    Halfway down, near the Liceu opera house, you walk over a round pavement mosaic by Joan Miró.

  7. 07
    Venue · 1908

    Palau de la Música Catalana

    Lluís Domènech i Montaner built it for the choral society Orfeó Català, and it opened in 1908. It is one of the few concert halls lit by daylight and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

    Look for

    On the street corner, Miquel Blay’s sculpture group celebrates Catalan folk song, with Saint George riding above the singers.

  8. 08
    Park

    Park Güell

    Eusebi Güell commissioned Gaudí to design a garden estate for wealthy families, but only two houses were sold. The city took it over and opened it as a public park in 1926.

    Look for

    Below the terrace, the forest of columns in the Hypostyle Room was meant to shelter the estate’s market.

  9. 09
    Museum · 1963

    Picasso Museum

    The museum opened in 1963 and focuses on Picasso’s formative years, including his time in Barcelona as a young man. It later expanded into several neighbouring palaces on the same street.

    Look for

    Step into the courtyards: each medieval palace has an open-air stone staircase rising to its main floor.

  10. 10
    Church

    Sagrada Família

    Gaudí took over the project in 1883 and worked on it until his death in 1926; he is buried in the crypt. Still unfinished, it was consecrated as a basilica in 2010.

    Look for

    Compare the two facades: the Nativity side, crowded with carved life, is Gaudí’s own; the gaunt, angular Passion side is by Josep Maria Subirachs.

  11. 11
    Church · 1383

    Santa Maria del Mar

    It was built between 1329 and 1383, remarkably quickly for its time, by the sea-faring people of the Ribera quarter. Porters carried stone down from Montjuïc for it, and they are remembered on the main doors.

    Look for

    Beside the church, the Fossar de les Moreres is a former cemetery for defenders who died in the siege of 1714, marked by a curved red memorial.
